title: Spectra
body:
Spreading light out by wavelength produces a **spectrum**, and its pattern reveals what
produced the light. Three types occur, and Kirchhoff's rules say which appears when.

```
continuous   an unbroken rainbow            hot dense object: a filament, a stellar interior
emission     bright lines on darkness       hot thin gas: a neon sign, a nebula
absorption   dark lines across a rainbow    cool thin gas in front of a hot dense source
```

The lines fall at wavelengths fixed by the atom producing them, because an electron moving
between two energy levels emits or absorbs exactly the energy difference. Those wavelengths are
a fingerprint, so hydrogen produces the same pattern in a laboratory and in a star 100 million
light-years away.

A star shows an absorption spectrum. Its dense interior emits a continuous spectrum, and its
cooler outer atmosphere removes specific wavelengths on the way out, which is why the dark
lines identify the elements present in that atmosphere. Helium was found in the Sun's spectrum
before it was found on Earth, which is the demonstration that the method works.

A spectrum therefore carries composition, temperature through
[[Blackbody Radiation|the shape of its continuum]], and motion through
the [[Doppler Effect|shift of its lines]]. Nearly everything in this course
was extracted from those three.
